bug_semantics: When proxy memory is enabled, the proxy treats the caller-controlled x-headroom-user-id header as the authoritative memory partition key without authenticating or otherwise binding that value to the caller. A remote client can select a victim identifier, causing memory search results to be injected into the attacker's LLM context and memory tool operations to read, create, update, or delete records in the victim's partition; this is a CWE-639 confidentiality and integrity failure.
flaw_origin: Commit da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 first integrated persistent memory into the network proxy and wrote memory_user_id = headers.get("x-headroom-user-id") in headroom/proxy/server.py, then passed that untrusted value directly to search_and_format_context and handle_memory_tool_calls. The pre-existing reference docker-compose configuration already bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787, and the BIC added no caller authentication or identity binding, so the new partition selector was remotely attacker-controlled in the shipped deployment model.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object says author 'chopratejas <chopratejas@gmail.com>' and committer 'chopratejas <chopratejas@gmail.com>'; its message contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5vg3-c628-vf56 describes direct x-headroom-user-id reads in OpenAI chat/Responses/WebSocket paths and cross-user memory reads/writes; https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/pull/2207 identifies this as WEB-02 from the v0.29.0 assessment and says the fix replaces six duplicated reads with resolve_memory_identity. Introduction: `git log -L 1323,1323:headroom/proxy/server.py da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192` attributes the added line `memory_user_id = headers.get("x-headroom-user-id")` exactly to da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192. That BIC's headroom/proxy/server.py passes the value into search_and_format_context (memory disclosure through injected context) and handle_memory_tool_calls, while the newly added headroom/proxy/memory_handler.py forwards user_id to backend search/save/update/delete operations. `git grep -n x-headroom-user-id 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 --` returns no match, directly verifying absence in the immediate parent tree; the parent docker-compose.yml already has command ["--host", "0.0.0.0"] and ports ["8787:8787"]. History: 787f9252041045c5d14337745e728657e0ecafbf made the header optional but continued trusting any supplied value; e8ab444f09e981343c2a77ce88ef7725a9a54656 moved the behavior during the server-to-handler split; cd1f0a2b9acdcad6bb1575599e2efcf5e3f66aea duplicated it into OpenAI chat and Gemini; c2451296df406bf8de4d678aa3cf1cb326738557 added the OpenAI Responses path; 82301bbf76679a0ff0c8fb907112be368424f932 added the WebSocket path. Fix: direct branch commit ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f introduces headroom/proxy/identity.py for WEB-02; merged PR commit 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 replaces the direct reads in headroom/proxy/handlers/{anthropic,gemini,openai}.py with resolve_memory_identity, which honors a header only for a local caller and otherwise selects a proxy-token-derived or OS-user identity. Its immediate parent a3d9424de98c54cb5656d29a33de6fe673691aca still contains the four request.headers.get identity sites plus the WebSocket site. Version boundary: v0.2.15 has no x-headroom-user-id under headroom/proxy; v0.3.0 contains the vulnerable server.py read and is the first version-sorted tag containing the BIC. v0.36.0 still contains the direct reads at anthropic.py:1226, gemini.py:345, and openai.py:3163, 5200, 6982. `git tag --contains 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 --sort=v:refname` begins at v0.36.1, whose tag resolves to release commit 37faf2f24724370483b1819b0921c899791bedc7; therefore the repository-derived affected boundary is v0.3.0 through v0.36.0 and the patched boundary is v0.36.1, notwithstanding the advisory database's Unknown package ranges. BIC attribution: `git cat-file commit da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192` shows one parent, human author/committer chopratejas, and no trailers or AI marker.
reasoning: The authorization failure begins when persistent proxy memory first becomes addressable by a raw request header, not when the same expression is later copied to additional providers or moved into handler mixins. The line-level history and BIC diff make da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 the smallest reachable causal commit: it simultaneously adds the header-derived partition key and the read/write consumers, while a direct grep of its sole parent's tree proves that selector was absent. The large feature commit is a normal one-parent commit in the available history, not a merge, move, revert, backport, release commit, or reconstructable squash with smaller member SHAs, so there is nothing to decompose. Later commits preserve and broaden the same trust error into OpenAI chat, Responses, WebSocket, Gemini, and refactored Anthropic paths; they are propagation, not the root BIC. The security branch directly fixes WEB-02 in ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f, and the landed fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 centralizes identity resolution so a network caller cannot choose another partition. Tag membership brackets the first shipped vulnerable state and the first fixed release. Finally, the verdict considers only the BIC commit object: its human author/committer and trailer-free message provide no commit-object AI evidence, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI; AI disclosure on PR #2207 concerns the later fix and is intentionally irrelevant to BIC attribution.
